<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אייר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918380_theRebbe_210" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_99_D7_99_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918380_theRebbe_210__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the interpretation of the verse "Who would give you as a brother to me" in Likkutei Torah, distinguishing between its application to the righteous and to penitents, and reconciling different midrashic and Rashi's interpretations.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, it is explained in Likkutei Torah, in the discourse beginning "Who would give you as a brother to me,"</t>
    <t s="1">that "Who would give you as a brother to me" refers to the righteous,</t>
    <t s="2">and "I would find you"</t>
    <t s="3">"outside" refers to penitents.</t>
    <t s="4">And superficially, one could say,</t>
    <t s="5">that what is said in Likkutei Torah, that "Who would give you as a brother to me" refers to the righteous, is according to the Midrashic interpretation that "as a brother to me" is like Yosef to Binyamin,</t>
    <t s="6">unlike according to Rashi's interpretation that "as a brother to me" is like Yosef to his brothers,</t>
    <t s="7">the beginning of the verse also speaks of penitents.</t>
    <t s="8">But according to what was brought above from the Tzemach Tzedek, that this that the Midrash interprets it as Yosef to Binyamin</t>
    <t s="9">(and not as Yosef to his brothers)</t>
    <t s="10">is because the request is that the Holy One, blessed be He, erase our sins not through suffering,</t>
    <t s="11">it is seemingly understood,</t>
    <t s="12">that also according to the Midrashic interpretation the verse speaks of penitents,</t>
    <t s="13">and in Likkutei Torah it explains that "Who would give you as a brother to me" refers to the righteous.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the inner purpose of Yosef's descent to Egypt was to alleviate the exile by gathering holy sparks, and that the brothers' sale of Yosef, though a sin on their part, aligned with this divine intent.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, it is known</t>
    <t s="2">that the intention</t>
    <t s="3">(above)</t>
    <t s="4">of Yosef's descent to Egypt was in order that he gather all the holy sparks that were in Egypt,</t>
    <t s="5">and Yosef gathered all the money found in the land of Egypt,</t>
    <t s="6">and through this the exile would be eased for them.</t>
    <t s="7">For this, that Yosef's descent to Egypt was the cause of the Egyptian exile,</t>
    <t s="8">is in externality,</t>
    <t s="9">but in internality it is to the contrary,</t>
    <t s="10">that through Yosef's descent to Egypt the exile was eased.</t>
    <t s="11">For the decree was that they would be in exile for four hundred years,</t>
    <t s="12">and through Yosef descending to Egypt they were in the Egyptian exile only 210 years</t>
    <t s="13">(because through Yosef refining the sparks that were in Egypt before the Children of Israel descended to Egypt, they did not need to refine as much),</t>
    <t s="14">and moreover,</t>
    <t s="15">the difficulty of the bondage was only 86 years.</t>
    <t s="16">And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="17">that this that the tribes sold Yosef to Egypt,</t>
    <t s="18">was not only not contrary to the intention,</t>
    <t s="19">but to the contrary,</t>
    <t s="20">such was the supernal intention, that Yosef descend first to Egypt in order to ease the exile.</t>
    <t s="21">However, since they did not know the intention, therefore for them it was considered a sin.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contrasts two explanations of Yosef's descent—one where it caused the undesirable exile, and another where it eased it—and explains why Yosef told his brothers not to be distressed, as their act served a positive divine purpose.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And to note,</t>
    <t s="1">that superficially,</t>
    <t s="2">the above matter</t>
    <t s="3">[that this that the tribes sold Yosef to Egypt was according to the intention]</t>
    <t s="4">is,</t>
    <t s="5">superficially,</t>
    <t s="6">also according to the explanation</t>
    <t s="7">(as it is simply)</t>
    <t s="8">that the intention of Yosef's descent to Egypt was in order that through this there would be the Egyptian exile,</t>
    <t s="9">[as per the exposition of our Sages, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="10">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="11">"And He sent him from the valley of Chevron"].</t>
    <t s="12">However,</t>
    <t s="13">according to this explanation,</t>
    <t s="14">through the tribes selling Yosef to Egypt, the exile was brought about,</t>
    <t s="15">an undesirable matter.</t>
    <t s="16">For although the intention of the Egyptian exile was in order that through this they would merit receiving the Torah,</t>
    <t s="17">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="18">the exile itself is an undesirable matter.</t>
    <t s="19">In contrast, according to the explanation that through Yosef's descent to Egypt the exile was eased,</t>
    <t s="20">this that the tribes sold</t>
    <t s="21">(brought down)</t>
    <t s="22">Yosef to Egypt is a desirable matter</t>
    <t s="23">(and their sin was only because this was not their intention).</t>
    <t s="24">And based on this, we can explain what Yosef said to the tribes,</t>
    <t s="25">"And now, do not be distressed and do not be angry with yourselves that you sold me here, for it was for sustenance that G-d sent me before you."</t>
    <t s="26">For superficially,</t>
    <t s="27">behold, all sins</t>
    <t s="28">(even though they are contrary to the supernal will)</t>
    <t s="29">are by divine providence and by His will, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="30">and nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="31">since the performance of the sin by a person is through his free choice</t>
    <t s="32">[and as explained in many places</t>
    <t s="33">that supernal providence</t>
    <t s="34">(regarding matters of Torah and mitzvos)</t>
    <t s="35">does not contradict the matter of choice],</t>
    <t s="36">it follows that the sinning person has harmed himself and therefore it is fitting for him to weep and lament over his sins,</t>
    <t s="37">so why did Yosef say to his brothers, "Do not be distressed and do not be angry with yourselves"?</t>
    <t s="38">And the explanation of this can be said,</t>
    <t s="39">that regarding all sins,</t>
    <t s="40">the matters that a person does are undesirable things,</t>
    <t s="41">contrary to the supernal will.</t>
    <t s="42">For although from this that even sins are by divine providence one must say that there is intention in them,</t>
    <t s="43">the intention is not in the sins themselves, heaven forbid, but in this that through the sins one will later come to repentance,</t>
    <t s="44">but the sins themselves are contrary to the supernal will,</t>
    <t s="45">and therefore one must weep and lament over them.</t>
    <t s="46">But this that the tribes sold Yosef to Egypt,</t>
    <t s="47">since the intention in this is</t>
    <t s="48">(not in order that they do repentance over this,</t>
    <t s="49">but the intention is)</t>
    <t s="50">in the descent itself,</t>
    <t s="51">"for it was for sustenance that G-d sent me before you"</t>
    <t s="52">[and particularly according to what was brought above, that through Yosef's descent to Egypt the exile was eased,</t>
    <t s="53">one could say that this matter is hinted at in the continuation of Yosef's words in the verse,</t>
    <t s="54">"And G-d sent me before you to place for you a remnant in the land"],</t>
    <t s="55">therefore, "do not be distressed... that you sold me here."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
